samples.summary: Empty-group drop discards XML whose production already mutated writer state, so a child's already-registered relationship (external hyperlink / image media) can survive with nothing referencing it
samples.evidence: `groupToXml` now serializes all children first (line 115) and then throws the result away (line 122). Child serialization is not side-effect-free: `elementToXml` → `resolveImageRId` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/index.ts:318) and `resolveHyperlinkRId` (index.ts:330) both call `writer.addRel(slidePath, ...)`, and the hyperlink one registers an attacker-influenced, `TargetMode="External"` target taken from document content. Today no serializer both registers a rel and returns '' (checked shapeToXml/textElementToXml/tableToXml/imageToXml — the image case returns '' only when no rel was added), so the reachable consequence is nil; the weakness is that the new discard-after-side-effect pattern makes the invariant "XML dropped ⇒ no rel registered" load-bearing without asserting it. If it ever breaks (e.g. a future text serializer that emits nothing for an empty block, or a table that returns '' after a cell registered a link), the shipped .pptx would carry an unreferenced external relationship pointing at a document-author-chosen URL that no visible element accounts for — a link in the package a reader/tooling can still follow. Attacker path would be: author a deck whose only content in a group is a link-bearing element that serializes empty, export, and the URL ships in slideN.xml.rels invisibly.
searchedFor: read export/pptx/group.ts, index.ts, zip.ts, slide.ts, image.ts, shape.ts, text.ts, animation.ts

finding.summary: Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: review: every credential in the pool (2) was retired — nothing left to fail over to

verdict.reason: The "finding" is not a claim about code — it is verbatim the repo's own review-harness diagnostic. `poolExhaustedError` at scripts/agent/ask.mjs:630-637 builds exactly "`${label}: every credential in the pool (${pool.size}) was retired — nothing left to fail over to`", and `lensFailureSummary` at scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:1690-1696 prefixes a thrown lens error with "Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: ". Concatenated with label="reviewer" and pool.size=2 they reproduce the finding text character-for-character; scripts/agent/ask.test.mjs:302 asserts that exact string. So the item reports that a review lens crashed before emitting a verdict because the reviewing agent's own API credentials were all retired (documented as the INFRA path in docs/tasks/active/20260820-fixer-live-credential-todo.md:8-11). It names no file, line, operation, or attacker-controlled input, and asserts no defect in the code under review. I also checked the only plausible security angle — credential leakage through this failure path — and it is absent by construction: the message interpolates only `label` and the integer `pool.size` (ask.mjs:632), the infra branch at review-panel.mjs:1697-1709 deliberately refuses to interpolate `err.detail` because doing so once published a credential, and the other branch applies `redactSecrets` (review-panel.mjs:1695). Nothing here is an authorization gate, secret exposure, injection sink, or broken crypto check.
